title: One-input proper support reduction identity
statement: Fix D,C,E,n,d,hl,o,z as in [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and the coordinates of [def-sf-integral-proper-projection-coordinates]. For a proper f:X→Y and a constructible integral K on X, supportReduction at the identity-open compactification, followed by system direct image of openIdentity on reduction K, equals reduction of the datum properIdentity component at K, followed by the mate-defined direct comparison at K. There is one input, and neither tensor nor projection occurs.

proof.text: Use the proved support-reduction normalization to make supportReduction invertible. Its composite with proper image of the canonical open identity is therefore an isomorphism from the reduction of the integral support value. Postcompose both candidate maps with its inverse. They are now maps between reductions of the same constructible integral object.

proof.text: Reconstruction is the inverse of the actual reduction-limit unit on constructible objects. Unit and counit naturality and the triangle identities give an explicit fully faithful reduction functor on this subcategory. Lift maps between reductions using that unit, limit of the map and inverse reconstruction. Equality after every system evaluation implies equality of every finite reduction of these lifts by naturality of reductionEvaluation. The integral joint-faithfulness theorem then identifies the lifts and hence the system maps.

proof.text: Paste the integral-to-finite coefficient adjunction comparison with finiteDirectAdjunctionNormalization. The existing unary pullback-evaluation theorem gives the square of left-adjoint comparisons. Transpose under the finite adjunction. Naturality and the two supplied counit equations give the square of right-adjoint comparisons, identifying evaluation of direct with the specified finite direct comparison.

proof.text: Finite evaluation of canonical identity-open cancellation gives the proper identity evaluation square. Paste this with the proved finite coordinates of the support adjunct. The coefficient properIdentity equation and finiteProperNormalization give the same endpoint composite for reduction of the integral proper identity followed by the direct mate. Cancel the finite endpoint isomorphism. Apply the detection result to the maps after postcomposition with the inverse support/open isomorphism, and cancel that inverse.

lean.statement:
theorem integralProperSupportReductionIdentity
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E]
    {n : ℕ} {hn : 1 ≤ n} (d : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn)
    (hl : IsUnit (C.l : D.k)) (o : Operations C.l E) (z : Realizations C.l E D o)
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f.hom.left]
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left) :
    supportReduction D C E d.higher hl o z f (.ofIsProper f.hom.left) K ≫
        (Operations.push C.l E o f.hom.left).map
          ((openIdentity o z X.obj.left).hom.app ((reduce X).obj K)) =
      (reduce Y).map ((d.higher.integral.properIdentity f).hom.app K) ≫
        (direct d.higher hl o z f).app K
